note: THE-342 fixes one defect wearing three costumes: a read that presents a PARTIAL or a FAILED result as if it were the whole truth. CoursePage made ten unbounded getDocs calls and swallowed every rejection into `catch { console.error }`; AdminCourses capped the shared catalogue at a hardcoded 200 while CoursePage read the same collection unbounded; ChurchMap read every active church on Earth, unordered and unbounded, and rendered a failure as 'No verified churches found in your area'. Every read now goes through one shared module (src/utils/bounded-list-read.ts) that counts first with getCountFromServer, loads under a ceiling in orderBy(documentId()) order, and THROWS rather than resolving into an empty list. Digests are the state THE-342 LEAVES each file at, APPENDED to the accepted set rather than substituted for anyone else's entry: THE-333's two entries for ChurchMap.tsx stay valid and untouched, and `acceptedFor` unions them. Substituting is how main went red for everyone once. NO firestore.rules digest is recorded here, deliberately and emphatically: this ticket does not touch that file, and THE-333 and THE-341 each recording one is what turned THE-325 red. No composite index was added either — every read is a single equality `where` plus orderBy(documentId()), which is a prefix scan of an automatic (field, __name__) index, so firestore.indexes.json is byte-identical and nothing inert was shipped.

entries.why: THE-342 owns this change and it is confined to the churches READ and two new render states. The read was `getDocs(query(collection('churches'), where('status','==','active')))` with no limit and no order — every active church globally on every visit to the public finder, growing with every customer Harvest signs. It now goes through readBoundedList: an exact getCountFromServer total, then CHURCH_MAP_FETCH_LIMIT documents in orderBy(documentId()) order. Two states were added: `churchesTruncated` renders a 'Showing N of M active churches' Alert above the list, and `churchesFailed` renders a destructive Alert that is checked BEFORE the empty state, because 'No verified churches found in your area' is a claim about the world and rendering it for a query that threw is the exact lie AGENTS.md's Silent-Failure Rule names. NOTHING #476 owns was touched: `key={mapTheme}` still remounts the TileLayer (react-leaflet creates L.TileLayer once on mount and does not re-issue tiles when the url prop changes), the tile url is still tile.openstreetmap.org with no {s} and no {r}, the OSM attribution string is byte-identical, attributionControl is still not false, and the harvest-tiles-dark pane filter is unchanged. The gold and blue divIcon markers are untouched — they still carry the hardcoded #d4a017 and #3b82f6 in their template HTML, which predates this ticket and is reported rather than changed, since altering marker colour is a palette change and not a read fix. A geohash scheme was considered and REPORTED rather than built: it needs a backfill of every church document and a composite index, and firestore.indexes.json does not deploy. The four house emoji markers this ticket first wrote into its comments here were removed, because the-333-guards sweeps this file's RAW source for emoji and the repo's no-emoji rule applies to it.

THE-342 owns this change and it is FOUR `orderBy(documentId())` clauses and one docblock, with no other byte moved. Card 86bbnjmwk described a CRM list truncating at 500 contacts plus 1000 users; those numbers DO NOT EXIST as written and were not reintroduced — CRM_FETCH_LIMIT has been a single 1000 governing both collections and both scoping paths since THE-67, useCRMCounts already reports the true totals through getCountFromServer, and AdminCRM already says 'Showing N — this list is incomplete' on screen. What the card missed, and what this ticket fixes, is that all four reads were UNORDERED: an unordered limit(N) is served in __name__ order over random document ids, so the thousand rows were an arbitrary and unstable thousand and the same admin refreshing could be shown a different thousand people. 'Showing 1,000 of 1,240' was true about the number while saying nothing about WHICH. The ordering is free — every automatic single-field index is keyed (field, __name__), so where('tenantId','==',x) plus this ordering is a prefix scan of an index that already exists and NO composite index is added. No write, no Stripe path, no statement or receipt path, and no fetch shape changed; the scoping branch, the super-admin gate, the NO_TENANT_SCOPE_MESSAGE throw and the merge are all untouched. AdminCRM.tsx itself was NOT edited, so #482's collapsible payment-links disclaimer and its Contacts/Roles switcher fix are byte-identical.

THE-342 owns this change. All ten unbounded getDocs calls are gone: the direct getDocs import is removed entirely, which is what makes 'every read here is bounded' checkable rather than assumed. The three tenant ternaries keep their where('tenantId') exactly as they were — removing one would not leak, because the /courses, /authors and /categories rules dereference resource.data.tenantId and Firestore must prove a list readable from the query constraints ALONE, so an unfiltered list is rejected wholesale for anyone who is not a super admin. The unfiltered `else` branch is therefore a deliberate platform-admin path that succeeds only for a super admin (isSuperAdmin() short-circuits belongsToTenant without reading a document field) and a guaranteed permission-denied for everyone else; the defect was never a leak, it was that the rejection was swallowed and rendered as 'No courses found'. It now sets `coursesFailed`, which CourseLibrary renders as a destructive Alert INSTEAD of its empty state. The adopted catalogue courses moved from a full libraryCourses scan to a by-id read (readDocsByIds, chunked at Firestore's 30-value `in` ceiling), which is complete by construction — bounding the old scan would have made an adopted course whose id sorted past the ceiling vanish from the member app silently, a worse bug than the one being fixed. THE-282's progress and adoption model is untouched: applyCourseOverrides, adoptableCourses, mergeCoursesForMembers, mergeAuthors, mergeCategories, completedLessons and quizAttempts are all still called at the same points with the same arguments, and THE-282's own suite now asserts that by name rather than by diff.

THE-342 owns this change. The catalogue ceiling is no longer a hardcoded 200 but the shared LIBRARY_COURSE_FETCH_LIMIT that CoursePage also imports, so the two screens cannot drift into two truths about one collection again — the guard asserts neither file passes a numeric literal to limit(). Every listener gained orderBy(documentId()). The headline figure and the plan cap no longer count `courses.length` from a limit(100) read: both come from an exact getCountFromServer, the header prints NO figure when the count is unavailable rather than a zero, and the cap fails CLOSED when the count is unknown, matching the file's existing 'unknown plan falls back to the smallest cap' stance. Adopted courses are resolved BY ID rather than against the ceilinged catalogue listener, so an adopted course past the ceiling no longer disappears from 'Your courses' and from the plan arithmetic; the preview lookup falls back to the same by-id pool. Truncation and failure now render through the ui/alert primitive. Nothing about adoption POSTing through /api/courses/adopt, the NoTenantScopeError path, or the read-only rendering of adopted courses changed.

THE-342 owns this change and it is two new optional props and the states they render. `readFailed` renders a destructive Alert and is checked BEFORE the existing `filtered.length === 0` empty state, which is the whole guarantee: `courses` is [] in both cases, so an empty collection and an unreadable one are indistinguishable in the data and must be distinguished on screen. `notices` renders the shared 'Showing N of M' lines in a default Alert above the list. Both use the installed ui/alert primitive rather than a hand-rolled div; the `empty` primitive was rejected for the failure state because a fault dressed as an empty state IS the bug. The existing Empty block, the 44px category pills, the featured hero and its pre-existing star glyph are byte-identical, and both props default so every existing caller is unaffected.

THE-342 ADDS this file: the one mechanism for reading a list that might not fit, generalised from the #405 precedent already in form-answers.ts rather than copied into four screens. readBoundedList counts first with getCountFromServer (an unclamped aggregation, so `total` survives the ceiling) then loads under the ceiling in orderBy(documentId()) order, and returns `truncated` as a fact (rows.length < total) rather than a flag inferred from how a loop exited. readDocsByIds fetches exactly the named documents, chunked at Firestore's 30-value `in` ceiling, and is complete by construction. NEITHER CATCHES — a rejected read throws and the caller renders a failure, because returning [] here would rebuild the exact bug the module exists to remove. truncationNotice is the single sentence every surface shows, so no two screens word it differently. It deliberately does not reuse dashboard-data.ts's countedRead, which refuses rows entirely above its ceiling: a trend over a truncated set is not a weaker trend but a wrong one, whereas a list is still useful truncated provided it says so.

THE-342 owns this addition: three exported ceilings beside the collection names both course screens already import, and nothing else in the file moved. LIBRARY_COURSE_FETCH_LIMIT is the single number governing every browsable read of the shared catalogue, placed here rather than in either screen because the bug was two screens disagreeing about one collection — a second constant elsewhere would let that drift back silently, which is exactly how CRM_FETCH_LIMIT came to hold a 500 on one path and a 1000 on the other. TENANT_COURSE_FETCH_LIMIT and COURSE_LOOKUP_FETCH_LIMIT cover a tenant's own courses and the author/category lookup pools; the pools get the same count-first treatment rather than a bare limit() because a truncated author pool renders a course AUTHORLESS rather than short. LIBRARY_COURSE_COLLECTIONS, TENANT_COURSE_COLLECTIONS, collectionsFor and resolveWriteTenant are untouched.
